Commentary.Commentary: Back with the chase! The players of England are out there, and so are the two openers of South Africa, where Aiden Markram will open the innings alongside Ryan Rickelton. ​​​​​​Luke Wood has the new ball in his hands, and he will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

Records broken? Plenty. England smashed their highest-ever T20I total, 304/2, overtaking the 267/3 vs West Indies in 2023. Salt’s 141 not-out is now the highest individual T20I score for England, and he also joined the elite club with four international T20I hundreds. The 200 came up in just 12.1 overs - the fastest ever in T20Is. And their 166/1 after 10 overs is the highest power-packed start any side has ever managed. South Africa are the only team who have conceded 250-plus in T20Is thrice. Also, this is the highest T20I total by a Test-playing nation playing another Test-playing nation.

The finishing touch? By 12.1 overs, England had stormed past 200 - the quickest any team has ever done in T20Is. Salt kept blasting away, breaking his own record with the highest T20I score for England and went unbeaten for 141 in just 60 balls. The skipper, Harry Brook, joined him late and added fuel to the fire, ensuring England crossed the 300-mark with a death-overs carnage. We got to see pure dominance, and South Africa’s bowlers had no answers.

So, what happened with the toss decision? Markram won it, the only thing so far, and bravely chose to bowl first, but soon must have regretted it. England’s openers came out like rockets, as Jos Buttler raced to his 50 in just 18 balls, and Salt took one more ball and completed his fifty in 19 balls. The scoreboard read 100/0 in the Powerplay, and by the time Buttler fell for a blistering 83 off 30, the damage was already severe. Salt didn’t stop there, as he hammered the fastest-ever T20I hundred by an English batter in 39 balls. South Africa tried to fight back when Bjorn Fortuin grabbed two wickets after a poor start, but England’s relentless striking had already set the tone.

BREATHTAKING. BRUTAL. RELENTLESS. What a fiery innings that was from England! Their openers tore into South Africa’s bowlers with no mercy, smashing a gigantic 304/2 in Manchester - the third-highest total ever in T20I history. For South Africa, it was nothing short of a nightmare as their bowlers were taken apart from ball one.

This is bowled on a hard length and outside off, Harry Brook reaches out and slaps it over the cover region and into the deep as the batters scurry back for the second run. England end with a monster total of 304/2 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: The stage is set at Old Trafford in Manchester, where England is gearing up to face South Africa in the second T20I match of the series. The electric atmosphere is palpable, especially with the highly anticipated Manchester Derby in the English Premier League just around the corner this weekend. England's Jos Buttler and Phil Salt are ready to take on the South African bowlers, with Marco Jansen standing at his mark, poised to deliver the first ball and kick-start the proceedings.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Aiden Markram (C), Ryan Rickelton (WK), Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Dewald Brevis, Tristan Stubbs, Donovan Ferreira, Marco Jansen, Kagiso Rabada, Bjorn Fortuin (In place of Corbin Bosch), Kwena Maphaka, and Lizaad Williams.

England (Playing XI) - Phil Salt, Jos Buttler (WK), Jacob Bethell, Harry Brook (C), Tom Banton, Sam Curran, Will Jacks, Liam Dawson, Jofra Archer (In place of Jamie Overton), Adil Rashid, and Luke Wood.
TOSS - South Africa win the toss and their skipper, Aiden Markram, has elected to BOWL first.

Meanwhile, in the fourth match of the Asia Cup 2025 in Dubai, Oman's bowlers performed well in the first innings, but Pakistan's decision to promote Mohammad Haris to number three proved effective as he played an impressive 66-run innings. However, Pakistan's middle order collapsed, losing a couple of wickets in a cluster, which ultimately restricted their total to 160/7. Aamir Kaleem and Shah Faisal picked three wickets each, while Shakeel Ahmed was economical with only giving just 17 runs in his four overs. In their chase, Oman started positively with some good boundaries, but a surprising move to bring on part-timer Saim Ayub proved to be a masterstroke for Pakistan as he struck twice inside the Powerplay, leaving Oman in a tough position at 27/2 at the end of the fourth over.

On the flip side, South Africa's solid performance in the first game was led by Donovan Ferreira, Dewald Brevis and Aiden Markram, who contributed crucial runs. Brevis continued his impressive form from the ODIs with a quickfire 23 off 10 balls, while Markram smashed 28 off 14 balls. With Nandre Burger joining the squad, South Africa's bowling attack looks even more formidable. To clinch the series, they'll need to maintain their momentum, particularly in the powerplay overs, and effectively handle England's batting lineup. Will the Proteas clinch the series, or will the hosts level it with a game to spare? Let's find out. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

England's batting lineup faced significant challenges in the first game, with key wickets falling early. Phil Salt, Jacob Bethell, and Harry Brook failed to make a substantial impact, while Jos Buttler shone with a quick 25 off 11 balls. Sam Curran remained unbeaten on 10 off 3 balls. To bounce back, England needs to refine their batting strategy, build meaningful partnerships, and improve shot selection.

The second T20I match between England and South Africa is set to be an intense encounter at the Old Trafford Cricket Ground, Manchester. South Africa currently leads the three-match series by 1-0 after a thrilling win in the series opener, where they defeated England by 14 runs via the DLS method.
... MATCHDAY ...

England will look to level the series in the second T20I at Manchester, having fallen 1-0 after a rain-affected opener. The home side showed glimpses of their potential, with Jos Buttler’s 25 off 11 and a flurry of intent from the top order. Rain curtailed the first game, setting a 69-run DLS target from 5 overs, and England managed 54 for 5. The hosts will need to convert small moments into a coherent innings, with the middle and lower order contributing more consistently to earlier totals in this format. England’s batting depth remains a notable strength. Philip Salt, Harry Brook, and Jacob Bethell provide aggressive options at the top and middle, while Sam Curran and Tom Banton add ballast to the order. If one of the latter trio can anchor an over or two, England could accelerate through the middle overs and post a more competitive total. The recalled Jofra Archer adds pace variety if selected, though his form and fitness will influence selection decisions. Adil Rashid’s form with the ball gives England a trusted spin option, with the host attack also relying on the left-arm variation and all-round capabilities of Liam Dawson and Curran to tighten the middle overs. South Africa arrive buoyant after a dominant opener, where their batting looked balanced and their bowlers executed plans with precision. Aiden Markram and Ryan Rickelton anchored the innings, while Dewald Brevis and Tristan Stubbs supplied the late-innings explosiveness that keeps pressure on the fielding side. Brevis, in particular, has shown he can shift momentum rapidly, a trait that can unsettle England’s bowlers. On the bowling front, Marco Jansen and Corbin Bosch each claimed two wickets, while Kagiso Rabada’s edge remains fearsome for England’s top order. Kwena Maphaka and Lizaad Williams provide additional depth and variation to keep the chase honest. Jansen and Bosch’s ability to strike early in the innings will test England’s top-order resilience, while South Africa’s lower-middle order has shown the capacity to finish games with Brevis and Stubbs at the crease. If England can stabilise early and squeeze the middle overs, they have the firepower to defend of chase a modest total and if South Africa continue their disciplined performance, they could seal the series with another composed display. This surely promises to be a cracking contest.
